actions.action: Scratch test on several stems to check for green tissue
Bend test stems to check for flexibility
Inspect stems for swelling buds or new growth
Once new growth appears, prune only clearly dead stems
Check that the root crown is at or slightly above soil level
Pull gravel back and add 2 inches of pine bark or pine needle mulch, keeping it off stems
Water deeply during dry spells and summer, avoiding sogginess
Fertilize lightly with acid-loving plant fertilizer (e.g. Holly-tone) after it leafs out
Watch new leaves for yellowing with green veins indicating high pH
Check leaf undersides for lace bug speckling or dark spots
If stems are brown and brittle, check near the base for new shoots
